metadata.title: Non-Markovianity-assisted optimal continuous variable quantum teleportation

extraction_notes.note: The main text has no section headings (PRL format), so main-text nodes have section null; only the Appendix carries subsections.
The QBM master equation is numbered twice (Eq. 1 main text and Eq. 8 = \label{HPZEq} in Appendix A.1); only the first copy got a node and the \ref{HPZEq} citations were wired by hand from DP2.
problem or definition: the phase-optimized fidelity is introduced as a quantity but is a max over phi, so promoted to problem; ClP3 resolves it.
Appendix A.3 is a calculation spread over the section with no separately stated result; kept as one remark containing its equations.
claim or remark: these are conclusions read off numerical plots (figures not in source), kept as claims with rigor numerical.

The derivation's closing sentence 'Replacing Eq. (25) in Eq. (26) we finally obtain Eq.~(2) and Eq.~(3)' is detected as an author label '(2)' mid-sentence, which no step can start at; PP1 ends at Eq. (26) and that sentence is left outside, though it is what links PP1 to ClP1.
The abstract/summary restatements, figure captions, the appendix restatement of the high-temperature regime and of the log-negativity formula got no nodes.

nodes.statement: The shared resource mode sent to Bob is affected by a decoherence process during its propagation; it is schematized by a non-Markovian Quantum Brownian Motion (QBM) channel, described by the following master equation with time-dependent coefficients: fracdrhodt = & -fracihbar [H_0,rho(t)]-Delta(t)[hatx,[hatx,rho(t)]] + nonumber \\ & + Pi(t)[hatx,[hatp,rho(t)]] - igamma(t)[hatx,\hatp,rho(t)\]\;, where H_0 is the fee hamiltonian of the system, the coefficient gamma(t) represent the damping factor, Delta(t) and Pi(t) are the normal diffusion and the anomalous diffusion coefficients respectively, and hatx and hatp are the quadrature operators.
conclusions: The shared resource mode sent to Bob is affected by a decoherence process during its propagation; it is schematized by a non-Markovian Quantum Brownian Motion (QBM) channel, described by the following master equation with time-dependent coefficients: fracdrhodt = & -fracihbar [H_0,rho(t)]-Delta(t)[hatx,[hatx,rho(t)]] + nonumber \\ & + Pi(t)[hatx,[hatp,rho(t)]] - igamma(t)[hatx,\hatp,rho(t)\]\;, where H_0 is the fee hamiltonian of the system, the coefficient gamma(t) represent the damping factor, Delta(t) and Pi(t) are the normal diffusion and the anomalous diffusion coefficients respectively, and hatx and hatp are the quadrature operators.

nodes.statement: At any fixed given temperature and dimensionless time tau=omega_c t, the non-Markovianity parameter x that characterizes the scales of the system time evolution identifies with the ratio between the bath and the system frequencies x=omega_c/omega_0: for xll 1, the dynamics is non-Markovian, otherwise it falls in the Markovian regime.
nodes.raw_latex:
At any fixed given temperature and dimensionless time $\tau=\omega_c t$, the {\em non-Markovianity} parameter $x$ that characterizes the scales of the system time evolution identifies with the ratio between the bath and the system frequencies $x=\omega_c/\omega_0$:
for $x\ll 1$, the dynamics is non-Markovian, otherwise it falls in the Markovian regime~\cite{PhysRevA.70.032113, TorreAsym2017}.
